  "text": "A survey of the tall‑grass prairie across a central U.S. region identified several vegetation patterns. The most widespread low‑land community is dominated by a single tall grass that often makes up more than 80 % of the plant cover; a second, similar grass occurs with it but is far less important. In wet, poorly aerated soils a reed‑like grass forms dense, nearly pure stands, while two other grasses create a smaller intermediate low‑land type. The most extensive upland community is led by a coarse, bunch‑forming grass that outweighs all other upland species combined; a different grass dominates steep slopes in the northern part of the area.
